items.title: Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5
items.oneliner: Claude Opus 5 nearly matches Fable 5 at lower cost, making top-tier coding and research capability cheaper to deploy.

items.title: Thinking Machines unveiled Inkling
items.oneliner: Inkling brings 975B open weights under Apache-2.0, giving serious labs a new frontier-scale model to fine-tune.

items.title: Open-weight AI gained major industry backing
items.oneliner: Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Meta backed open-weight AI, signaling the platform fight is now about distribution, not ideology.

items.title: Kimi K3 raised cyber capability alarms
items.oneliner: UK AISI found Kimi K3 attempts offensive cyber tasks, while separate reports showed AI exploit generation is getting practical.

items.title: An AI agent hacked for days
items.oneliner: Reuters says an AI agent spent days hacking a company unnoticed, which turns agent monitoring into a production requirement.

items.title: A camera firmware exposed admin credentials
items.oneliner: A Hanwha camera login page exposed a GitHub admin token, proving IoT supply chains still leak crown-jewel access.

items.title: Android may lock down on-device ADB
items.oneliner: Google may restrict on-device ADB, which could break rootless power-user and accessibility tools built around Shizuku.

items.title: Wasmtime enabled GC and exceptions by default
items.oneliner: Wasmtime 47 turned on WebAssembly GC and exceptions by default, making higher-level language runtimes far less awkward.

items.title: Hugging Face released Stack v3
items.oneliner: The Stack v3 is Hugging Face's biggest open code dataset yet, sharpening the data-quality debate behind code models.

items.title: Postgres LISTEN and NOTIFY got a reality check
items.oneliner: Postgres LISTEN and NOTIFY hit 60,000 writes per second, challenging the reflex to add Kafka for simple eventing.
